summary.oneLiner: Praveg has rapidly expanded its resort footprint to 825+ rooms and relaunched its high-margin event/advertising business, but H1FY26 losses were driven by fixed PPP lease costs, new property ramp-up, and seasonal closures; profitability is expected to rebound sharply in H2 due to festive season demand and full-year contribution from newly commissioned assets.

one-line thesis: Praveg has rapidly expanded its resort footprint to 825+ rooms and relaunched its high-margin event/advertising business, but H1FY26 losses were driven by fixed PPP lease costs, new property ramp-up, and seasonal closures; profitability is expected to rebound sharply in H2 due to festive season demand and full-year contribution from newly commissioned assets.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +28.94% YoY to INR77.71cr; EBITDA: INR10.17cr (margin compressed by 15-20pp due to fixed lease costs and new property OpEx); PAT (reported): -INR14.97cr; PAT (normalized): -INR14.97cr (no major one-offs beyond depreciation of INR15.98cr); Order Book: INR10cr+ from event/exhibition pipeline; Net Debt: INR10-15cr (mostly group loans, minimal bank debt)
guidance: Revenue growth: H2 to exceed H1 by >100% (historical seasonality + new revenue streams); Margin: EBITDA margin to improve to 25-30% in H2 due to operating leverage; Order inflow: INR50-70cr expected from events/advertising; Capex/commissioning: Thinnakara South (Dec 2025), Kutch expansion (Q1FY27), minimal new capex due to investor model
order book & pipeline: INR10cr+ from government and corporate events; 20+ weddings booked at Adalaj Theme Park; 252-bed Kutch asset awarded (equivalent to 126 rooms); ongoing bids for 5+ major exhibitions
segment / subsidiary detail: Hospitality & Events: INR26.29cr in Q2; Advertising: INR11.21cr in Q2; Adalaj Theme Park: opened Sep 25, 2025, generating wedding/event revenue; Bangaram: 25-30% Oct-Nov occupancy; Thinnakara North: operational, Thinnakara South: 80% complete; Kutch: 76 rooms operational, 126 new rooms from Varanasi relocation; Advertising: acquired Abhik & Bidhan, revenue INR24cr in H1, targeting INR50cr annual run-rate
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion via investor model (landowner + Praveg op) in Udaipur, Kihim, Kashi; potential museum/heritage tourism projects; government PPP bids for 5+ new destinations; digital advertising monopoly expansion in metro cities; international expansion into Africa
margins & cost dynamics: Fixed PPP lease costs (non-negotiable, same across seasons); high fixed labor cost (1,500+ in-house staff vs. outsourced); depreciation INR15.98cr in H1; incremental H2 margin contribution ~75% due to low variable costs; seasonal resorts closed in Q2 added cost without revenue
capex / expansion: H1 capex: ~INR41cr (mostly Thinnakara North, Adalaj); H2 capex: INR10-20cr (Thinnakara South completion); future capex: minimal due to investor model; Kutch expansion uses relocated Varanasi infrastructure (capex reduced to INR5-7cr for 126 rooms)
capital allocation: Prioritizing investor-funded expansion (70%+ future growth); minimal debt reliance (only INR10-15cr bank limits); retained earnings used for operational ramp-up; warrant forfeiture (INR500cr+) converted to reserves; no dividend policy announced
risks & watch-items: Seasonal revenue volatility (Q2 losses); PPP lease inflexibility; delayed CRZ clearances for Kihim/Kashi; reliance on government event tenders; high fixed labor cost structure; brand perception risk from vegetarian-only policy in luxury segment
management quality / tone: Confident, long-term oriented, defensive on financial guidance; emphasizes operational milestones over short-term P&L; dismisses stock price volatility as 'emotional'; highlights corporate governance and compliance; optimistic on H2 recovery and investor model scalability
non-obvious takeaways: Adalaj Theme Park’s 1M+ social media reach and wedding bookings represent a low-cost, high-margin experiential revenue stream beyond traditional rooms; Kutch expansion uses stranded Varanasi assets — effectively zero capex for 126 rooms; advertising revenue from Abhik & Bidhan is now larger than event management revenue and growing faster
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High fixed costs and seasonal losses | Praveg Limited | beneficiary | High | H2FY26 profitability surge from seasonal demand + new assets will validate operational model |
| Reliance on government event tenders | Abhik & Bidhan (subsidiary) | beneficiary | Medium | Advertising revenue growth is accelerating and less cyclical than events |

themes.title: Hospitality & travel up-cycle
themes.need: Q1FY27 split hotels from airlines. INDHOTEL delivered a 17th consecutive record quarter - consolidated revenue INR 2,419cr (+15%), EBITDA INR 753cr at 31.1%, standalone occupancy jumping to 82% from 76% on a 41.8% standalone EBITDA margin, and asset-light management-fee income INR 168cr (+26%) - with management now framing the West-Asia war as a NET tailwind because outbound travel stays home; leisure RevPAR (Rajasthan/Goa) ran up high-20s. Airlines got the mirror image: INDIGO's EBITDAR margin collapsed from 28.0% to 15.6% on blended ATF of ~INR 140-150/litre versus INR 85-90 pre-war (fuel CASK +~80% YoY), leaving yield as the only defence. MHRIL shows domestic leisure premiumisation is real - Keystone average unit realisation +73% to INR 14.4 lakh on stable gross sales. LEMONTREE/CHALET/SAMHI/THELEELA ride the same occupancy-led room cycle; TRAVELFOOD/TBOTEK/DREAMFOLKS remain levered to airport PAX and B2B travel.
themes.driver: Occupancy-led (not rate-led) RevPAR compounding plus INDHOTEL's Ginger conversion cadence stepping 15->20->25->40 per quarter through FY27; for airlines the swing is INDIGO's guided Q2 PRASK growth of 'more than 25%' on flattish capacity against ATF cracks.
